exercises.q: Не забуду-с, — откланивалась дама, ставшая ___ (доверчивый).
exercises.why: In both English and Russian adjectives and adverbs have three forms, which are called degrees: positive, comparative, superlative — good, better, best; fast, faster, fastest. The comparative degree of Russian adjectives is formed by adding "-ее" (sometimes shortened to "-ей") to the stem of the adjective: новый — новее; красивый — красивее. This comparative form is the same for all genders and the plural. It is not declined and can be used as a predicate only. Many adverbs which end in "о" are formed from adjectives … The comparative degree of these adverbs is formed in the same way as the comparative of adjectives: *Он идёт быстро. Я иду быстрее. Там было холодно. Здесь ещё холоднее. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 80, 82.  ·  From Фёдор Достоевский, «Идиот».
